$comment: Cover-sheet spec only. The component inventory — ids, sections, groups, captions and variants — lives next to the @Previews as @CatalogGroup / @CatalogComponent / @CatalogVariant annotations under glimmer-catalog/src/main/kotlin/ee/schimke/m3catalog/glimmer/, exactly as the sibling :catalog does. `referenceKits` names the Glimmer kit this sheet is compared against. Its "(Community)" suffix is the Figma Community channel Google publishes its kits through, not a third-party redraw — the Material 3 Design Kit this repository reproduces carries the same suffix — so `.design-parity.json`'s repo-wide `design-led` direction applies here unchanged. There is no `compareWith`: this sheet is rasterised by Robolectric while m3-catalog is rasterised by Skiko, so pairing the two would put a RENDERER difference into a comparison meant to be about design. `modes` is a single dark entry because Glimmer draws for an additive display where black is unlit — a light mode is not a thing the hardware can show — and the dark display surface keeps the preview server from staging these captures on white, which the additive-zero ground would vanish into. `display.hero` names the @Preview function `CardActionSticker` rather than the `Card` component. The hero is the one picture the sheet leads with, and `Card`'s own default cell is dominated by its header gradient, so the cover leads instead with the kit's action layer — the cell alpha19 puts on `ActionCard` rather than on `Card` — which shows a title, a body and a real Glimmer button. That cell publishes as the preview id `card__ideal__default__content-action`, but a hero resolves against componentIds and @Preview function names only (validate-catalog-spec, and the preview server's own lookup), so the function name is the token that names it.
